title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via unescaped route parameter in vhost example
analysis:
In `examples/vhost/index.js`, the route handler for `main.get('/:sub', ...)` extracts the route parameter `req.params.sub` and directly reflects it back to the client using `res.send('requested ' + req.params.sub)`. 

Data Flow:
- **Source**: Untrusted URL path parameter `:sub` accessed via `req.params.sub`, which is automatically URL-decoded by Express's router (`decode_param`).
- **Sanitization/Validation**: None. The parameter is concatenated directly into the response without HTML encoding or input sanitization.
- **Sink**: `res.send(...)`, which defaults to sending the response with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` when provided a string argument.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A victim visiting the following URL will execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the application:
```http
GET /%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C%2Fscript%3E HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com:3000
```
Response:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

requested <script>alert(document.domain)</script>
```

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via User-Agent Header
analysis:
Data flow trace: - Source: Untrusted HTTP request header `req.headers['user-agent']` captured in `app.use(function(req, res, next) { online.add(req.headers['user-agent']); next(); });` (line 32). - Sanitization/Validation: None. The `User-Agent` string is stored as-is without any validation, sanitization, or HTML entity escaping. - Sink: In `app.get('/', ...)`, `online.last(5, ...)` retrieves the user IDs (User-Agent strings) and passes them to `list(ids)` which builds raw HTML string `
  • ' + id + '
    • ` without HTML encoding. The result is then directly sent to the client via `res.send()` at line 53, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Conceptual Exploit Payload: Send an HTTP request with an XSS vector in the `User-Agent` header: ```http GET / HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost:3000 User-Agent: ``` When any user navigates to `GET /`, the response body renders: ```html

    Users online: 1

    ``` causing malicious JavaScript execution in the context of the user's session.
